info.title: Keasy API
info.description: Keasy host: identity, connections, vended credentials and the job record

get.summary:
Ready when the database answers. The identity provider's keys are not a
condition: a realm outage would otherwise restart every instance at once,
and requests already say `auth/keys-unavailable` on their own.

503.description: The database did not answer in time

post.summary:
Relay one chat completion to the gateway. The answer is streamed back as
the gateway sends it, byte for byte; a reader who leaves drops the stream,
and with it the upstream request. A refusal of the gateway's own — a spent
budget, an upstream failure — arrives in the protocol's error format, with
its status.

200.description: The gateway's answer as it streams: OpenAI chat completion chunks (`text/event-stream`), ended by an error event carrying `gateway/silent` if the gateway goes quiet mid-answer, or one completion (`application/json`)

400.description: Not an alias, or a malformed request

502.description: The AI gateway could not be reached

504.description: The AI gateway did not begin its answer in time

400.description: No such secret, or a URL it does not reach

403.description: A sink by anyone but an admin

409.description: A connection of that name, or a second sink

504.description: The store did not answer the probe in time

409.description: Jobs wrote their output to it; `dependents` names them

504.description: The store did not answer the probe in time

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description:
A folder under the connection's prefix (`dynamic/`, `a/b`), to list
only what is under it. No `.` or `..` segments.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many objects: 1000 when left out, and never more.

200.description: The first `limit` objects under the connection's prefix, or under `prefix` within it

400.description: Not a storage source, or a prefix that leaves it (`data.field`)

504.description: The store did not answer in time

post.summary: LIST a source, WRITE and DELETE under the sink.

200.description: The probe's report, stored with the connection

504.description: The store did not answer the probe in time

get.summary:
Every dataset the workspace produced, for anyone in it: each is opened by
reading its job's corpus.

200.description: Every completed job's output, newest first

post.summary:
A job begins as a draft, always: what it runs, where it lands. Submitting
it is the one way a job comes to run.

201.description: The draft, created; `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/submit` makes it the job to run

400.description: The destination is not a sink, or the name or folder is misspelled (`data.field`)
The name or folder is misspelled (`data.field`)

200.description: The job's saved dashboard, or null when none is saved

put.summary: The dashboard is the job's: who may change the job may save it.

400.description: The spec is not a JSON object

413.description: The spec is larger than a dashboard may be

post.summary:
The runner's one report: `running` starts the run and, sent again, renews
its lease — a running job no report has renewed for the lease (60 s) is
swept as `job/abandoned`; an end records how the run ended, and dates it.
`completed` stores the run report verbatim, unread.

204.description: Recorded: the run started, its lease renewed, or its end

400.description: The job is a draft, which is never run, or the status is not running or an end

409.description: The job has already ended (`job/ended`): the sweep's `job/abandoned` among them

post.summary:
A draft becomes the job to run, in place: the edits, the folder check and
the promotion are one write, so a refusal leaves the draft as it was and a
success leaves no draft behind. The only way a job comes to be pending.

202.description: The draft is now the job to run, under the same id

400.description: The name or folder is missing or misspelled (`data.field`)

409.description: Not a draft (`job/not-draft`), or another job writes to that folder already (`job/folder-taken`; the job stays a draft, unchanged)

200.description: The secrets, with the connections using each; never a secret's value

post.summary:
An editor creates one, for a source or, as an admin, for the sink; any editor
may use it in a connection, and its creator or an admin changes it.

409.description: A secret of that name exists

504.description: The store did not answer the probe in time

403.description: Neither its creator nor an admin

409.description: Connections still use it; `dependents` names them

patch.summary:
Rotation replaces the whole spec, and is committed only if every connection
using the secret still validates with the new one.

403.description: Neither its creator nor an admin

422.description: A connection using it would not validate with the new spec; `dependents` names them

504.description: The store did not answer the probe in time

post.summary: Probe the secret through every connection that uses it.

200.description: The probe's report, stored with the secret

403.description: Neither its creator nor an admin

504.description: The store did not answer the probe in time

post.summary:
Vend a credential over `scope` for `access`. Anyone in the workspace reads a
completed job's dataset. An editor reads a source connection — Unity
Catalog's temporary path credentials over an external location — to build
a job, and writes a job's dataset while it runs, if they may change that job.

200.description: A credential that opens the scope's prefix, and only it, for an hour

400.description: Not a storage source, or an access the scope does not give

403.description: A source read below editor; a job written below editor, or by someone who may not change it

404.description: No such connection, or no such job

409.description: A job read before it completed (`job/not-completed`), or written before it runs (`job/not-running`) or after it ended (`job/ended`)

504.description: The store, or the identity service before it, did not answer in time

Access.description: What a vended credential lets its holder do under its prefix.

Alias.description:
A model, by what it is for. Which upstream answers is the gateway's
configuration (`infra/ai/`), so nothing here names a provider.

Branding.description:
How this instance looks, as its deployment declares it (`KEASY_BRANDING_FILE`).
Public: the web reads it to render the login page and the first paint,
before anyone has signed in.

default.description: The family a visitor starts with; absent leaves the web's own.

families.description:
The theme families members may choose among; empty allows every
shipped theme.

lock.description: Members wear the default and choose nothing.

logo.description: The mark the shell shows: a URL or a path the web serves.

organization.description:
The Keycloak organization this instance serves, by alias
(`KEASY_ORG_ALIAS`): which entry of a session's organizations is this one.

theme_css.description: A theme stylesheet to inline on every page.

messages.description: The conversation, in the OpenAI message format.

can_modify.description:
Whether the caller may change or delete it: the sink is an admin's,
any other connection its creator's or an admin's.

name.description: What programs write after `@`, and the connection's key.

oneOf.description:
The folder under the sink the output lands in. A draft may leave it
out; it needs one, no other job's, to be submitted.

sink_connection.description: Where the output lands: the sink connection's name.

probe_url.description:
A storage URL to LIST before the secret is stored. A secret has
no location of its own, so without one it is only checked to build a
client.

Dashboard.description:
A job's saved dashboard. `spec` is the dashboard the web's BI kit
serialises (`DashboardSpec`): keasy stores it and hands it back, and never
reads a field of it.

updated_by.description: Keycloak `sub` of the member who saved it last.

Dataset.description:
A completed job's output: where its corpus is, and when it was written.
What the corpus holds is the corpus's own to say — a reader opens it (with
a credential vended for the job) and asks its `fossil_tables` and
`fossil_columns`; keasy keeps no copy of it.

id.description: The job that wrote it, which is the scope its read credential is asked for.

Direction.description: A source is read through `@name/…`; the one sink is where job output lands.

DraftEdits.description: Edits to a draft: as it is written (PATCH), and as it is submitted.

oneOf.description:
The draft's folder under the sink, spelled as on create. Submitting
needs one, unless the draft holds one already.

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every 4xx/5xx, and the payload of an SSE `error` frame — the
shape fossil's problems have: a code, its fixed title, a detail for a
person that nothing parses, and the data the code carries.

ErrorCode.description:
Every error the server answers with. Closed: a code the server does not
declare here cannot be sent, and the web keys its copy by this enum.

One grammar with fossil's and kanzo-ui's codes, `area/kind`, so one registry
in the web keys all three. The areas are keasy's own and never one of
fossil's (`storage`, `engine`, `run`, …): a code means one thing. Each
variant is its wire name spelled in Rust, `area/kind-x` as `AreaKindX`, so
the code a test asserts and the variant a handler names are one word.

Every refusal the server writes is an [`ErrorBody`] with one of these, with
one exception: the AI relay (`routes::ai`) passes the gateway's own refusal
through in the OpenAI error format the browser's model client reads, status
and body untouched. Its own failures — unreachable, silent —
are `gateway/*` bodies like any other.

ErrorData.description: What a refusal carries beside its words.

after.description:
How long a deadline waited before it fired, in milliseconds: set on
the `*/silent` codes, and only on them.

dependents.description:
What the refusal is about: what still uses a secret or connection,
or the connections a rotation would break.

field.description:
The request field the refusal is about, so a form can say it on that
field: `folder`, `name`.

FileEntry.description: One object under a connection's prefix.

FileListing.description: The objects under a connection's prefix, the first `limit` of them.

truncated.description: More objects lie under the prefix than were listed.

can_modify.description:
Whether the caller may change, run or delete this job, worked out for
each response: the interface draws what this says and does not
re-derive it.

created_by.description:
Keycloak `sub` of who created the job: with an admin, the one who may
change, run or delete it. Everyone in the workspace reads it. Taken from
the token, never the body.

oneOf.description:
The folder under the sink the output lands in. A draft may not have one
yet; every other job does, and no two of them share one in a sink.

heartbeat_at.description:
The job's lease: taken when it is submitted, renewed by every
`running` its runner reports. A job whose lease lapses is swept.

problem.description:
Why a `Failed` run failed, as the browser that ran it reported it: a
problem (`{ code, title, detail, data, … }`), stored verbatim and
**opaque** — the web branches on its `code`, the server never does.

report.description:
What the run reported, verbatim and **opaque**: fossil's run report
(`RunReport`, `{dest, dropped}`). keasy stores it, hands it back and
never reads a field of it — the last time a host re-typed this struct,
it ended up asking for `vertex/<Type>.parquet`, a file the layout pass
deletes. What the corpus holds is the corpus's to say: a reader opens
it and asks its `fossil_tables` and `fossil_columns`.

sink_connection.description:
The sink connection the output lands in, under `{sink.url}/{folder}`,
reached with a credential vended from that connection's.

JobFolder.description: The folder a job's output lands in under the sink: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or digit.

JobStatusReport.description:
What the runner reports of a job's run (POST `/v1/jobs/{id}/status`): that
it runs, again every so often to hold its lease, and how it ended. The
browser runs the program (`@fossil-lang/executor`) and writes the output
with a credential vended for the job; keasy only records.

problem.description:
Why the run failed (on `failed`): the run's problem, stored verbatim
and opaque.

report.description: fossil's run report (on `completed`), stored verbatim and never read.

status.description:
`running` (the first time it starts the run, every time after it renews
the lease), or the end: `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

spec.description: The dashboard, as the web serialises it: any JSON object.

ResourceName.description: A credential's, a connection's or a job's name: no leading or trailing whitespace, and no `/`, `@`, `\` or control character.

Role.description: A role this application declares on its Keycloak client.

oneOf.description: A source connection's prefix, by the connection's name.

connection.description: A source connection's prefix, by the connection's name.

oneOf.description: A job's dataset, by the job's id.

job.description: A job's dataset, by the job's id.

Scope.description: What a credential is asked for: fossil's `Scope`, verbatim.

endpoint.description: MinIO, R2 or a gateway. An `http://` endpoint opts into plain HTTP.

external_id.description:
AWS's guard against the confused deputy, when the role's trust
policy asks for one.

role_arn.description:
The role keasy assumes to vend a credential scoped to one prefix.
AWS needs it. With an endpoint and no role, keasy asks for
`arn:aws:iam::000000000000:role/keasy-vended`; a store that validates
roles (Ceph RGW, SeaweedFS) needs that role declared, or this set.

SecretSpec.description: A secret's spec as a request states it, its values included.

SecretSpecView.description: A secret's spec as a response shows it: what names it, never what signs with it.

can_modify.description:
Whether the caller may change or delete it: its creator or an admin.
Any editor may use it in a connection; its value is never returned.

used_by.description: The connections that use this secret.

url.description: The prefix the connection is: `s3://bucket/prefix/` or `az://container/prefix/`.

ThemeChoice.description: One theme: the `data-theme` value it is selected by, and its display name.

ThemeFamily.description: A theme as a pair: what it is called by day and by night.

UpdateSecretRequest.description:
A rename, a rotation or both. `spec` replaces the whole spec, secrets
included, and is stored only if every connection using the secret
still validates with it.

ValidationReport.description: One probe of a credential or a connection, check by check.

VendedCredential.description:
A credential scoped to one prefix, for a lifetime — Iceberg REST's
`StorageCredential`, keys and all (`s3.access-key-id`, `s3.session-token`,
`s3.session-token-expires-at-ms`, `adls.sas-token.<host>`, …), so any
reader of vended credentials reads it. Handing it out is the point, so
this is the one response type that carries a secret: its values stay
[`SecretString`] until the moment they are written into the response.

prefix.description: The canonical prefix it opens, ending in `/`.

storage_credentials.description: One per prefix; a reader picks the longest prefix that holds a path.

Forbidden.description: The caller holds no role this route admits

KeysUnavailable.description: The identity provider's keys are unreachable

RateLimited.description: The caller exceeded their request rate
